recipes.name: Mom's Easy Creamed Chipped Beef on Toast
ingredients_raw: 12 ounces beef lunch meat (such as Carl Buddig ®)

steps.text: Whisk milk, flour, salt, and pepper together in a large bowl until smooth.
Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Gradually stir in milk mixture until thick. Add beef; cook and stir until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Pour beef mixture over toast to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Easy Creamed Chipped Beef on Toast
raw_recipe.description: This easy creamed chipped beef on toast features a simple sauce of milk, flour, and butter combined with deli-style roast beef served over toast.

review.reviewBody: It important that you use Carl Budding Beef and not roast beef as AR added into the review page narrative. You can also you dried salted beef but you must omit the salt from the recipe and soak your beef to remove some of the salt (not as quick and easy). I use 2 heaping tablespoons of flour per cup of milk (AR calculates that at about 3/4 cup). They changed my directions also. Add the entire milk mixture to butter and whisk constantly until thickened (5-7 min). For thinner cream chipped beef use pre warmed milk before adding the flour for thicker use cold milk.

This is a good start for a good breakfast gravy. The changes I made were to cook the Carl Budding beef in a couple tablespoons of butter and then remove the beef from the skillet. Pour a quart of fat free half-and-half into the skillet and heat it up. Mix a couple tablespoons of cornstarch with water to thicken the half-and-half -- omit the flour (avoid that flour after taste to the gravy and lumps). Add a couple more tablespoons of butter to the gravy, along with cooked beef and the salt and pepper. Serve over homemade biscuits for a good old fashioned breakfast. Every mouthful brings back memories of days gone by.

I like this recipe because it uses a milk gravy base for its body. I fry chopped up dried beef in 1/4 cup of butter till slightly browned. I omit the flour and use two heaping tablespoons of corn starch disolved into the milk. I omit salt all together beause Dried beef is generally salty enough. You will never get lumps using cornstarch.
When its thick and bubbly, I pour it over homefries or toast. And, splash on some Tabasco!

I just made this, totally impressed!! Using Carl Budding is genius: it's shaved really thin, not too strongly flavored, and extremely cost effective. I did melt the butter first, lightly cook some chopped onion, then slowly add the milk. Eliminated the salt and threw in a couple twists of cracked pepper. Before this the only way I knew to find creamed chipped beef was in the frozen food aisle from Stauffer's, this was WAY better

SHAZSK, ls 100% right. No. Just no. This recipe is incorrected titled. I'm sure it is a fine recipe for Creamed, Chipped, Cold Cut Beef. The recipe for Creamed Chip Beef calls for "dried beef" which has a different taste and texture than beef cold cuts. Dried beef has been around since before refrigeration. It is made of a lean cut of beef brined in salt and, at least in the olden days, could be kept off ice for a long time. This is why the U.S. military has used it to provide protein to our service personnel for generations. Today, it is sold primarily by Armour and Hormel in a jar but you may also find it in a bag with lunchmeat. When you choose to make your family Chipped Beef, please consider doing so the authentic way with dried beef as your grandma and great grandma did. Just be sure to thoroughly rinse the salt off before cooking. It is part of our heritage and history so let's use the correct main ingredient. Make it with cold cuts, if you choose, but give it another name.

I minced a small amount of onion, melted butter in pan, & cooked the onion a little to soften. I then put rest of ingredients in, and also added a little garlic powder, but did leave out the salt. It can always be added later to taste. Very good comfort food!

I made this for brunch this a.m. and Hubby & I loved it! I did tweak it a bit, however (I can't help myself): I added pinches of smoked paprika & cayenne, and a dash of Worcestershire, along with some sautéed shallots & mushrooms. We were out of bread so I served it over crispy hash browns. YUM.

This is very similar to what I have done for many years. But I melt the butter and saute the jar dry beef (sliced), and also saute chopped onion. Sometimes for variations, I have added such items as diced green chilies to the cream gravy. It is a wonderful quick and tasty meal. I generally have it for a quick dinner and serve over biscuits. My mother made this frequently when I was growing up and served on toast; therefore I highly recommend trying it!

Traditionally we cooked it like making a roux, using one part butter to one part flour. We fried the diced Buddig beef in the butter and then added flour (we didn't usually take the beef out) and cooked the flour mix a bit before slowly whisking in the liquids and other ingredients to the consistency you want. Also, for a traditional touch, don't forget the dusting of nutmeg *Chef's Kiss*

Absolutely LOVE LOVE LOVE this recipe for my DH and I. Have made it many times. He just likes a little more of a "zing" so I add a little McKormick minced onion and minced garlic, and I increase the pepper to 1/2 tsp. He loves it! (Great on potatoes too)
Just as I remember
I'm with Gee Gee. Add chopped up boiled eggs and it's even better. You can also omit the dried beef and just use the eggs. It's great either way.
I like this recipe on Pancakes. I like a thinner consistency to the sauce.

This is the way my mom made it. I don't care for the dried beef version. Not sure why. We called this SOS. We called it SOS when we used hamburger instead of lunchmeat also. Pretty sure everyone knows what it stands for.
This was very good and easy. It didn’t last long! Will definitely make again.

Great easy recipe. 
Much better than store bought heat and served. 

Made as directed except I don't use salt.
It was delicious. First time ever making! Definitely saving under favorites. So simple!

So I don't usually post but I've gotta say love the ease of this recipe, everyone in my house loves it... 
with the creamed chipped beef I add a little worcestershire sauce.. I also use this for my sausage biscuit breakfast but use of course ground sausage first fried and crumbled up and use fresh ground pepper to give it more of that sausage gravy taste and again love this recipe.

After reading the reviews, I thought I had been making chipped beef incorrectly. After tasting this recipe I will stick to making a roux. I just didn't like the taste. No matter how long I cooked it all I could taste was flour. But to each their own. I'll stick with my Grandmothers recipe.
